# Wally

Wally is a browser and extension interaction recorder. It records browser actions and extension popups (any chrome-extension://) via Chrome CDP, captures clicks, fills and navigations, and exports standalone Playwright test scripts with HAR network capture.

- Site: https://cxto21.github.io/wally/
- GitHub: https://github.com/cxto21/wally
- Author: Ignacio del Corro
- License: BSD-3-Clause

## What is Wally

Wally attaches to Chrome via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) on port 9222. It records user interactions on any website and on extension popups/pages, then generates reproducible Playwright scripts. Optional HAR capture stores network traffic for debugging.

## Key features

- Record: clicks, fills, navigations, and chrome-extension:// popup interactions
- Exec: run arbitrary Playwright JavaScript live against the attached Chrome (page, context, browser)
- Network capture: CDP Network domain -> network.jsonl and HAR 1.2 (network.har)
- Export: standalone Playwright test file from recorded actions
- Daemon: background recording with status, stop and summary
- Works with any website and any Chrome extension

## Installation

```bash
npm install playwright
node wally.js daemon start --url https://example.com
node wally.js daemon start --profile "Profile 9" --url https://avnu.fi
node wally.js daemon start --har
node wally.js daemon status
node wally.js daemon stop
node wally.js export
node wally.js exec "return await page.title()"
node wally.js exec "await page.getByRole('button', {name: /Approve/}).click()"
```
